= Christian Denominations Reconciliation =

== Participants ==
* [[User:TPROCKOPHD|TPROCKOPHD]] - Tyler T. Procko, Ph.D.
* Codex from OpenAI

== Description ==

This project explores how Wikidata represents a small selection of Christian church bodies. It is an investigation of knowledge organization, rather than an effort in ecumenics or a count of all denominations worldwide.

'''Research question: How does Wikidata classify the selected 19 churches?'''

For each selected church (a small set of 19 for brevity), I examine what it is classified as, how those classifications connect to broader classes, and whether a query for Christian denominations finds it. I compare the records to identify common patterns, meaningful differences, and possible modeling issues. Some differences may reflect church structure or scale rather than errors.

The related-entry tables and exploratory queries below provide background. The main investigation is the individual review of 19 selected records, summarized in one comparison table at the end.

== Related Entries Already Present on Wikidata ==

As an initial foray into this project, some time was spent with manual searching/exploration, and parallel sub-agent workflows of Codex models to find related entries already present within Wikidata.

These tables collect starting points for exploring how Wikidata represents Christianity and its denominations. The groupings organize the project, and the Type column gives working descriptions for investigation. Comments record relevance and questions for later queries.

Timestamps describe Wikidata record revisions, recorded on 29 October 2026; Z denotes UTC. N/A marks resources or placeholder rows without a Wikidata entity record.

== Exploratory queries ==


This section includes a query-driven exploration of Wikidata given the related terms given earlier. Nothing prescriptive; just exploratory queries.

=== Instances of any Christian Denomination ===
{{SPARQL
|label=Run this query
|query=
SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT ?denomination) AS ?count)
WHERE {
  ?denomination wdt:P31/wdt:P279* wd:Q879146.
}
}}

This includes instances of Christian denomination and instances of any subclass of it. For direct instances, we get 1,367 results; for indirect instances, we see a total of 1,670 results, on 29 October 2026 (UTC). These results count records satisfying the selected relationships in Wikidata. They do not establish a complete count of denominations worldwide. The query does not filter for present-day existence or location, and does not separately include classes connected only through subclass-of statements. Its results depend on the coverage and modeling of the underlying data, including how denominational families and named church bodies are classified.

We can expand this a bit with different values, as Wikidata modelers can sometimes use different terms. 

=== Alternate Classifications ===
The original query follows classification links to Christian denomination (Q879146); it does not search for the word denomination. Alternative labels for that same item are already covered. Additional candidates may have different classifications, such as Christian movement, Christian organization, or church congregation.

This query compares direct instance-of classifications. It counts each item once within each class. Items can occur under multiple classes, so these counts overlap and should not be added together.

{{SPARQL
|label=Run the classification comparison
|query=
SELECT ?class ?classLabel ?count
WHERE {
  {
    SELECT ?class (COUNT(DISTINCT ?item) AS ?count)
    WHERE {
      VALUES ?class {
        wd:Q879146 wd:Q123129246 wd:Q995347
        wd:Q94670589 wd:Q2638480 wd:Q34651
      }
      ?item wdt:P31 ?class.
    }
    GROUP BY ?class
  }
  SERVICE wikibase:label { bd:serviceParam wikibase:language "en". }
}
ORDER BY DESC(?count)
}}

Results recorded on 29 October 2026 (UTC):

|-
! Classification !! Direct instances
|-
| {{Wikidata entity link|Q2638480}} || 1,991
|-
| {{Wikidata entity link|Q879146}} || 1,367
|-
| {{Wikidata entity link|Q94670589}} || 648
|-
| {{Wikidata entity link|Q34651}} || 248
|-
| {{Wikidata entity link|Q995347}} || 87

| {{Wikidata entity link|Q123129246}} || 47

The denomination count here is the direct-instance count of 1,367, comparable with the narrower version of the first query.

=== Anything with a Christian Religion/Worldview ===

{{SPARQL
|label=Run this query
|query=
PREFIX wd: <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/>
PREFIX wdt: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct/>

SELECT (COUNT(DISTINCT ?item) AS ?count)
WHERE {
  ?item wdt:P140/wdt:P279* wd:Q5043.
}
}}

This returns 388,732 items on 29 October 2026 (UTC). We can expand this query to get the types of things with this religion/worldview and their counts:

{{SPARQL
|label=Run this query
|query=
PREFIX wd: <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/>
PREFIX wdt: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct/>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>

SELECT ?type ?typeLabel ?count
WHERE {
  {
    SELECT ?type (COUNT(DISTINCT ?item) AS ?count)
    WHERE {
      ?item wdt:P140/wdt:P279* wd:Q5043;
            wdt:P31 ?type.
    }
    GROUP BY ?type
  }
  OPTIONAL {
    ?type rdfs:label ?typeLabel.
    FILTER(LANG(?typeLabel) = "en")
  }
}
ORDER BY DESC(?count) ?type
}}

This query examines items whose religion or worldview (P140) value is Christianity (Q5043) or a subclass of Christianity. It groups those items by their directly stated instance of (P31) types, without restricting the subjects to organizations.

The full query returned 2,330 distinct types on QLever. The table below selects types relevant to investigating denominations, movements, organizations, and local church communities. It is an exploratory selection rather than a ranking of the largest categories, the largest of which was "church building" with 133,065 results.

Each count includes only items satisfying the affiliation condition. An item with several direct types can contribute to several rows, so these counts overlap and should not be summed. They are not totals for all instances of the listed classes. Items without a qualifying P140 statement or the required subclass path are omitted. Items without a directly stated P31 value also do not appear in this breakdown.

== The 19 selected churches ==

The selection grew out of exploratory browsing and the earlier query results, with additional named Baptist, Catholic and Eastern Orthodox examples chosen for comparison. These are the 19 records selected for this project; the list is not a random or representative sample of Christianity.

The Catholic Church, Eastern Orthodox Church and the selected Protestant bodies differ in structure and scale. Including them together allows those differences to be examined without assuming they should all have identical classifications.

== Querying the selected records ==

This query lists the direct instance-of classifications returned for each selected record and checks whether the record matches the path <code>instance of / subclass of*</code> to Christian denomination. In plain terms, this query asks if Wikidata classifies these churches as Christian denominations, either directly or through a more specific type.

{{SPARQL
|label=Check the 19 selected churches
|query=
PREFIX wd: <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/>
PREFIX wdt: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct/>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>

SELECT ?church ?name ?type ?typeLabel ?foundByDenominationQuery
WHERE {
  VALUES (?church ?name) {
    (wd:Q3555519 "Presbyterian Church in America")
    (wd:Q1149100 "Presbyterian Church (USA)")
    (wd:Q922480 "Church of Scotland")
    (wd:Q626416 "Presbyterian Church in Korea (TongHap)")
    (wd:Q329646 "United Methodist Church")
    (wd:Q3066164 "Free Methodist Church")
    (wd:Q1189165 "Church of the Nazarene")
    (wd:Q1128669 "Lutheran Church of Australia")
    (wd:Q940272 "Ethiopian Evangelical Church Mekane Yesus")
    (wd:Q1351880 "Southern Baptist Convention")
    (wd:Q2422454 "Assemblies of God USA")
    (wd:Q104319 "Seventh-day Adventist Church")
    (wd:Q198745 "United Church of Canada")
    (wd:Q1089816 "Church of South India")
    (wd:Q5415680 "Evangelical Free Church of America")
    (wd:Q463455 "American Baptist Churches USA")
    (wd:Q496651 "National Baptist Convention, USA")
    (wd:Q9592 "Catholic Church")
    (wd:Q35032 "Eastern Orthodox Church")
  }
  OPTIONAL {
    ?church wdt:P31 ?type.
    OPTIONAL {
      ?type rdfs:label ?typeLabel.
      FILTER(LANG(?typeLabel) = "en")
    }
  }
  BIND(EXISTS {
    ?church wdt:P31/wdt:P279* wd:Q879146.
  } AS ?foundByDenominationQuery)
}
ORDER BY ?name ?type
}}

=== Reading the results ===

The results contain '''33 rows for 19 distinct churches'''. Each row is a church–type pair. When a church has several returned instance-of values, it appears on several rows. Those rows do not represent additional churches.

'''Multiple types are not automatically inconsistent.''' For example, an item can be both an organization and a Christian denomination. The individual reviews consider whether the classifications describe compatible aspects of the same entity, mix different senses of a name, or introduce an inappropriate level of organization.

In this result set, 16 of the 19 records match the denomination query and three do not:
* {{Wikidata entity link|Q5415680}} — Evangelical Free Church of America.
* {{Wikidata entity link|Q3066164}} — Free Methodist Church.
* {{Wikidata entity link|Q1128669}} — Lutheran Church of Australia.

A false result means the record does not match this particular query; it is not a judgment that the church is not a denomination. Conversely, a true result does not prove that its classification is appropriate.

The Church of Scotland is a useful case to examine: it matches the query although none of its returned direct types is Christian denomination. Its inclusion therefore depends on the class hierarchy. The review below identifies two such paths, through national Church and state church.

These are the direct P31 values returned through <code>wdt:</code>, which uses best-ranked statements. Preferred and deprecated statements on the item page may affect what is returned. The table below records the results of the query above; it is not a transcription of every statement at every rank. In particular, when preferred statements exist for a property, normal-ranked statements for that property are omitted from its wdt: values; deprecated statements are excluded.

== Individual reviews ==

These are limited classification reviews, not complete audits of church history, governance, or every Wikidata claim. The linked item revisions document the statements inspected. External sources are used for selected questions of identity or scope. The subclass observations use the following class revisions.<ref name="class-revisions">Inspected Wikidata class revisions: [https://www.wikidata.org/w/index.php?title=Q879146&oldid=2555522898 Christian denomination (Q879146), revision 2555522898]; [https://www.wikidata.org/w/index.php?title=Q94670589&oldid=2561145032 Christian organization (Q94670589), revision 2561145032]; [https://www.wikidata.org/w/index.php?title=Q1530022&oldid=2561263477 religious organization (Q1530022), revision 2561263477]; [https://www.wikidata.org/w/index.php?title=Q163740&oldid=2558758526 nonprofit organization (Q163740), revision 2558758526]; [https://www.wikidata.org/w/index.php?title=Q1649443&oldid=2503039949 national Church (Q1649443), revision 2503039949]; [https://www.wikidata.org/w/index.php?title=Q2325038&oldid=2547031193 state church (Q2325038), revision 2547031193]; [https://www.wikidata.org/w/index.php?title=Q4204511&oldid=2555705853 historic Church (Q4204511), revision 2555705853]; [https://www.wikidata.org/w/index.php?title=Q2638480&oldid=2561435083 church congregation (Q2638480), revision 2561435083]; [https://www.wikidata.org/w/index.php?title=Q346575&oldid=2504582959 Protestant church (Q346575), revision 2504582959].</ref>

For each record, the review makes short notes on:
# What the item describes and whether its label or description is ambiguous.
# Its instance-of values and relevant broader classes, including the path responsible for inclusion in the denomination query where one exists.
# Whether the modeling is reasonable, questionable, or unclear, with a source or concrete statement supporting the observation.

Classifications, organizational parts, affiliations and historical relationships should be interpreted according to their own meanings. A difference between two items is a question to investigate, not by itself an error.

=== Presbyterian Church in America ===

{{Wikidata entity link|Q3555519}}

The record has a direct instance-of statement to Christian denomination, so it matches without needing a subclass step. Its classification matches that of Presbyterian Church (USA), but these remain separate items. Sharing a class does not imply that two church bodies are identical.<ref name="record-Q3555519">[https://www.wikidata.org/w/index.php?title=Q3555519&oldid=2547707505 Wikidata Q3555519, revision 2547707505], inspected 30 October 2026 (UTC).</ref>

=== Presbyterian Church (USA) ===

{{Wikidata entity link|Q1149100}}

The record is directly an instance of Christian denomination and therefore matches. Comparing it with Presbyterian Church in America illustrates a limit of this query: it groups the two bodies under the same type but does not explain their institutional differences or history. No conflict is apparent from this type alone.<ref name="record-Q1149100">[https://www.wikidata.org/w/index.php?title=Q1149100&oldid=2549123291 Wikidata Q1149100, revision 2549123291], inspected 30 October 2026 (UTC).</ref>

=== Church of Scotland ===

{{Wikidata entity link|Q922480}}

The returned types are nonprofit organization, national Church, and state church. Both national Church and state church have a direct subclass-of statement to Christian denomination, so either supplies the required path. These are two paths to one church, not two denominations. The Church’s own account describes it as national and spiritually independent of state control. The state church classification therefore needs interpretation against the meaning of that class; the successful query match does not establish that the classification is appropriate.<ref name="record-Q922480">[https://www.wikidata.org/w/index.php?title=Q922480&oldid=2545864439 Wikidata Q922480, revision 2545864439], inspected 30 October 2026 (UTC).</ref><ref name="scotland-structure">[https://www.churchofscotland.org.uk/about-us/our-structure Church of Scotland: Our structure], consulted 30 October 2026 (UTC).</ref>

=== Presbyterian Church in Korea (TongHap) ===

{{Wikidata entity link|Q626416}}

The TongHap item is directly an instance of Christian denomination and matches. The identifying qualifier matters: this review concerns this particular Korean Presbyterian body, not every church with a similar English name. The type establishes its place in the query but does not establish equivalence with other Presbyterian items.<ref name="record-Q626416">[https://www.wikidata.org/w/index.php?title=Q626416&oldid=2450492319 Wikidata Q626416, revision 2450492319], inspected 30 October 2026 (UTC).</ref>

=== United Methodist Church ===

{{Wikidata entity link|Q329646}}

The record is directly an instance of Christian denomination and matches. This gives a useful comparison with Free Methodist Church: the query finds this item directly but misses the other item, whose returned denomination type is broader. That difference is about recorded classification and cannot by itself be used to rank their legitimacy as denominations.<ref name="record-Q329646">[https://www.wikidata.org/w/index.php?title=Q329646&oldid=2534305684 Wikidata Q329646, revision 2534305684], inspected 30 October 2026 (UTC).</ref>

=== Free Methodist Church ===

{{Wikidata entity link|Q3066164}}

The returned types are religious denomination and organization, and the record does not match. Religious denomination is broader than Christian denomination: being an instance of the former does not entail membership in the latter. This explains why the query cannot simply infer a match from that type. A possible improvement is a supported, more specific classification of the item; changing all religious denominations into Christian denominations would be incorrect. Before proposing an edit, the scope of this item should also be checked against national and worldwide Free Methodist bodies.<ref name="record-Q3066164">[https://www.wikidata.org/w/index.php?title=Q3066164&oldid=2534534227 Wikidata Q3066164, revision 2534534227], inspected 30 October 2026 (UTC).</ref>

=== Church of the Nazarene ===

{{Wikidata entity link|Q1189165}}

The record has a direct Christian denomination classification and matches. It therefore follows the same retrieval pattern as United Methodist Church. The query does not distinguish theological traditions within that shared class; those would require additional properties and a separate question. No inconsistency follows from the single returned type.<ref name="record-Q1189165">[https://www.wikidata.org/w/index.php?title=Q1189165&oldid=2555664646 Wikidata Q1189165, revision 2555664646], inspected 30 October 2026 (UTC).</ref>

=== Lutheran Church of Australia ===

{{Wikidata entity link|Q1128669}}

The returned types are religious denomination and religious organization, and neither supplies a successful path in the query results. The church’s own website describes the Lutheran Church of Australia and New Zealand as a Christian denomination. This supports treating the result as a discovery gap worth reviewing, rather than evidence that the body is not Christian. A more specific instance-of statement is a candidate improvement, subject to confirming the item’s scope and a suitable reference.<ref name="record-Q1128669">[https://www.wikidata.org/w/index.php?title=Q1128669&oldid=2406928235 Wikidata Q1128669, revision 2406928235], inspected 30 October 2026 (UTC).</ref><ref name="lca-about">[https://www.lca.org.au/about-us/ Lutheran Church of Australia: About us], consulted 30 October 2026 (UTC).</ref>

{{Wikidata entity link|Q940272}}

The record directly uses Christian denomination and matches. In contrast with Lutheran Church of Australia, it does not depend on the query inferring Christian identity from a broader religious type. This is a difference in retrieval coverage, not evidence that the two institutions have the same organization or that one is a more authentic denomination.<ref name="record-Q940272">[https://www.wikidata.org/w/index.php?title=Q940272&oldid=2558025424 Wikidata Q940272, revision 2558025424], inspected 30 October 2026 (UTC).</ref>

=== Southern Baptist Convention ===

{{Wikidata entity link|Q1351880}}

The record directly uses Christian denomination and matches. The word Convention in its name is not an obstacle because the query follows statements rather than searching labels for the word church or denomination. Whether this body’s governance is adequately represented requires examining other properties; the present test establishes only its classification and retrieval.<ref name="record-Q1351880">[https://www.wikidata.org/w/index.php?title=Q1351880&oldid=2551025390 Wikidata Q1351880, revision 2551025390], inspected 30 October 2026 (UTC).</ref>

=== Assemblies of God USA ===

{{Wikidata entity link|Q2422454}}

The USA record directly uses Christian denomination and matches. The scope indicated in the label matters when comparing results: a named national body should not automatically be merged with a similarly named international body. The present result establishes a match for this item, not a count of all Assemblies of God bodies worldwide.<ref name="record-Q2422454">[https://www.wikidata.org/w/index.php?title=Q2422454&oldid=2492842000 Wikidata Q2422454, revision 2492842000], inspected 30 October 2026 (UTC).</ref>

=== Seventh-day Adventist Church ===

{{Wikidata entity link|Q104319}}

The returned types are organization, Christian denomination, and Christian organization. The direct denomination statement supplies the match. Christian denomination is itself a subclass of Christian organization, which is a subclass of religious organization and then organization in the inspected hierarchy. The additional direct types therefore overlap with broader classifications already reachable from the specific type; they do not by themselves create a contradiction.<ref name="record-Q104319">[https://www.wikidata.org/w/index.php?title=Q104319&oldid=2561338755 Wikidata Q104319, revision 2561338755], inspected 30 October 2026 (UTC).</ref>

=== United Church of Canada ===

{{Wikidata entity link|Q198745}}

The returned types are nonprofit organization, organization, and Christian denomination. The denomination statement supplies the match. Organization is also a superclass of nonprofit organization, so those two assertions overlap. Nonprofit status and denominational identity describe different aspects of the same item and are not inherently inconsistent. This review has not independently audited its legal status.<ref name="record-Q198745">[https://www.wikidata.org/w/index.php?title=Q198745&oldid=2534309643 Wikidata Q198745, revision 2534309643], inspected 30 October 2026 (UTC).</ref>

{{Wikidata entity link|Q1089816}}

The record directly uses Christian denomination and matches. Its inspected English label is Anglican Church of South India, while the project uses Church of South India. The World Council of Churches describes a union involving Anglican, Methodist, Presbyterian, and Congregationalist predecessors. The label therefore deserves review for whether it communicates the whole body adequately. === Evangelical Free Church of America ===

{{Wikidata entity link|Q5415680}}

The query returns religious organization, which is preferred-ranked. The item also has a normal-ranked Protestant church statement; it is omitted from the wdt:P31 results because a preferred statement exists for that property. A separate rank-aware check found no subclass path to Christian denomination from either type. Removing the rank preference alone would therefore not fix this missed match. EFCA describes itself as an association of autonomous churches. Its broad organizational type is understandable, but a more specific classification would require an explicit decision about how such associations fit the denomination class.<ref name="record-Q5415680">[https://www.wikidata.org/w/index.php?title=Q5415680&oldid=2518360748 Wikidata Q5415680, revision 2518360748], inspected 30 October 2026 (UTC).</ref><ref name="efca-sof">[https://www.efca.org/sof Evangelical Free Church of America: Statement of Faith], consulted 30 October 2026 (UTC).</ref>

{{Wikidata entity link|Q463455}}

A uniform number of direct types is not necessary for comparable retrieval.<ref name="record-Q463455">[https://www.wikidata.org/w/index.php?title=Q463455&oldid=2401714249 Wikidata Q463455, revision 2401714249], inspected 30 October 2026 (UTC).</ref>

The difference is redundant explicit typing rather than an obvious conflict.<ref name="record-Q496651">[https://www.wikidata.org/w/index.php?title=Q496651&oldid=2433965508 Wikidata Q496651, revision 2433965508], inspected 30 October 2026 (UTC).</ref>

{{Wikidata entity link|Q9592}}

The returned types are church congregation, Christian Church, historic Church, and Christian denomination. The direct denomination statement supplies the match. The class’s definition and the statement’s evidence must settle that question. The number of types alone is not grounds for deleting any of them.<ref name="record-Q9592">[https://www.wikidata.org/w/index.php?title=Q9592&oldid=2555386640 Wikidata Q9592, revision 2555386640], inspected 30 October 2026 (UTC).</ref>

{{Wikidata entity link|Q35032}}

Historic Church is also a subclass of Christian Church, so those two types overlap in the inspected hierarchy. Sharing these types with the Catholic Church does not establish identical institutional structure. The classification query groups the records but leaves that structural comparison unresolved.<ref name="record-Q35032">[https://www.wikidata.org/w/index.php?title=Q35032&oldid=2551602112 Wikidata Q35032, revision 2551602112], inspected 30 October 2026 (UTC).</ref>

== Common themes and conclusions ==

'''The 19 records are classified in several ways, and those choices affect whether a denomination query finds them.'''

* '''Direct versus inherited membership.''' Fifteen records have a direct Christian denomination type. Church of Scotland is the sixteenth match, through national Church and state church. Three selected records do not match. These are outcomes for this selected sample, not an estimate of all denominations.
* '''Broader types can hide relevant candidates.''' Free Methodist Church and Lutheran Church of Australia are typed as religious denominations, but the query requires Christian denomination or a subclass of it. A subclass path goes from narrower to broader classes; it does not let a query infer that every religious denomination is Christian. The Lutheran church’s own description makes this a concrete candidate for a more specific, referenced classification.<ref name="lca-about" />
* '''Multiple types are not automatically errors.''' Organization, nonprofit organization, and Christian denomination can describe compatible aspects of one entity. Some broad types are also reachable through subclass paths, so stating them directly can repeat information. Requiring every church to have the same number of types would not improve the model by itself.
* '''Ranks change what the query displays.''' EFCA’s preferred religious organization statement hides its normal-ranked Protestant church statement from wdt:P31 results. However, the rank-aware check found no qualifying subclass path from either type. Rank explains the missing displayed type, but does not by itself explain how to make the record match.<ref name="record-Q5415680" />
* '''A successful match is not a complete modeling verdict.''' Church of Scotland’s state church classification, the Anglican wording in Church of South India’s label, and Catholic Church’s church congregation type each raise questions that the denomination count cannot settle. These require examining definitions, scope, and supporting sources rather than declaring every difference a mistake.

The practical result is a distinction between '''being described as a Christian denomination''' and '''being retrievable by this particular Wikidata path'''. Improving retrieval may involve a more specific statement, a justified hierarchy correction, or clearer item scope. It should not involve forcing all selected churches into identical organizational descriptions.

This is a deliberately selected comparison of 19 records. It does not measure the prevalence of modeling issues across Wikidata, determine a worldwide denomination total, or establish that every selected item ought to be classified identically. No item edits are proposed as established corrections on the basis of this review alone.

== Limitations: does starting with instance of miss anything? ==

The main query asks: '''Does Wikidata classify this church body as a Christian denomination, directly or through a more specific type?'''

The path <code>wdt:P31/wdt:P279*</code> first follows '''instance of''' from a particular church body to its type, then follows '''subclass of''' upwards to broader types. The star allows zero subclass steps, so a direct instance-of statement to Christian denomination is sufficient.

For example:
* Presbyterian Church in America → instance of → Christian denomination.
* Church of Scotland → instance of → national Church → subclass of → Christian denomination.

This assumes that the selected church body is modeled as an '''instance'''. An item connected to Christian denomination only by subclass-of statements would not match. That alternative path treats the item as a '''class''', so it asks a different question: is this item a kind of Christian denomination?

=== Testing the assumption on our 19 records ===

The following query compares both routes without changing the sample. <code>P279+</code> requires at least one subclass step; using <code>P279*</code> alone would also allow Christian denomination itself to match without any step.

{{SPARQL
|label=Compare instance and subclass routes for the 19 churches
|query=
PREFIX wd: <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/>
PREFIX wdt: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct/>
SELECT ?church ?name ?viaInstance ?viaSubclass WHERE {
VALUES (?church ?name) {
    (wd:Q3555519 "Presbyterian Church in America")
    (wd:Q1149100 "Presbyterian Church (USA)")
    (wd:Q922480 "Church of Scotland")
    (wd:Q626416 "Presbyterian Church in Korea (TongHap)")
    (wd:Q329646 "United Methodist Church")
    (wd:Q3066164 "Free Methodist Church")
    (wd:Q1189165 "Church of the Nazarene")
    (wd:Q1128669 "Lutheran Church of Australia")
    (wd:Q940272 "Ethiopian Evangelical Church Mekane Yesus")
    (wd:Q1351880 "Southern Baptist Convention")
    (wd:Q2422454 "Assemblies of God USA")
    (wd:Q104319 "Seventh-day Adventist Church")
    (wd:Q198745 "United Church of Canada")
    (wd:Q1089816 "Church of South India")
    (wd:Q5415680 "Evangelical Free Church of America")
    (wd:Q463455 "American Baptist Churches USA")
    (wd:Q496651 "National Baptist Convention, USA")
    (wd:Q9592 "Catholic Church")
    (wd:Q35032 "Eastern Orthodox Church")
  }
 BIND(EXISTS { ?church wdt:P31/wdt:P279* wd:Q879146 } AS ?viaInstance)
 BIND(EXISTS { ?church wdt:P279+ wd:Q879146 } AS ?viaSubclass)
}
ORDER BY ?name
}}

'''The alternate route does not recover any of the three missed records in this sample.''' Free Methodist Church, Lutheran Church of Australia, and Evangelical Free Church of America are false for both tests. This establishes a result for these 19 records; it does not establish that the starting assumption is harmless everywhere in Wikidata.

=== Looking beyond the sample ===

This query finds items that reach Christian denomination through subclass-of statements but do not match the original instance-based path. It is a discovery query, not a validated count of additional church bodies.

{{SPARQL
|label=Find subclass candidates missed by the instance-based route
|query=
PREFIX wd: <http://www.wikidata.org/entity/>
PREFIX wdt: <http://www.wikidata.org/prop/direct/>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
SELECT DISTINCT ?candidate ?label WHERE {
 ?candidate wdt:P279+ wd:Q879146.
 FILTER NOT EXISTS { ?candidate wdt:P31/wdt:P279* wd:Q879146 }
 OPTIONAL { ?candidate rdfs:label ?label. FILTER(LANG(?label) = "en") }
}
ORDER BY ?candidate
}}

The run returned '''58 distinct items'''. Selected examples illustrate why they need review:

{| class="wikitable"
! Item !! Why it matters for interpreting the result
|-

'''More matches do not automatically mean a better denomination count.''' Combining the routes would mix classes with instances unless each candidate’s meaning is checked. A subclass statement alone does not prove a modeling error, and a named item alone does not establish that it represents one distinct denomination. These 58 items should therefore be treated as review candidates, not added uncritically to a denomination total.

Both queries use best-ranked <code>wdt:</code> statements and the endpoint’s current data. They do not test every possible affiliation, part-of relationship, or statement rank. Results can change as statements and subclass hierarchies are edited.
